title: Runs skipped at recovery or failed in the background stay visible
lead: From the S17 review, not fixed. A run skipped at daemon recovery stays non-final, and a failed background engine job is invisible to the owner (nothing records the failure on the run).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: From the S17 review, not fixed. A run skipped at daemon recovery stays non-final, and a failed background engine job is invisible to the owner (nothing records the failure on the run).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
- Per decision 116 (no new final state), a run whose Reconcile fails at recovery stays in the run manager. A stop on it answers with the run, not "no run" (TestRecoverySkipsBadRuns, kill case, rewritten).
- The skipped run's error shows on its wire row (EngineRun.Error) and in ork status and the Overview row. Its state is unchanged.
- A background job that returns an error keeps the error on the wire row in daemon memory; the state stays as the engine left it (new TestBackgroundErrorStaysOnTheWireRow).
- run.json has no error key after a failed background job (read the file back).
- The next job (retry, stop or approve) clears the error. A stop that cancels a busy job does not record context.Canceled as a failure.
- Healthy recovered runs and healthy background jobs are unchanged (existing TestRecoveredRunCanBeStoppedAndActiveRunIsPaused).

- Folded in from the S05 review (2026-10-20): recovery also skips a non-final run, queued or not, whose project is no longer registered (recoverRuns, "project ... is not registered"). The run is not in the run manager, so it cannot be stopped, yet activeRunsLocked counts it from the store and it holds the daemon up forever. Proposed test: such a run shows in the status with an error naming the missing project, does not block idle exit, and a stop answers (see Implement, Open).

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests first in internal/daemon/runs_test.go: change the kill case of TestRecoverySkipsBadRuns (:390-393, :416-423) so the run is kept and a stop answers; add TestBackgroundErrorStaysOnTheWireRow (runDaemon with a roundRunner that returns an error, run.start, waitState, then engineRuns shows Error and the run.json has no error key). Run go test ./internal/daemon -run 'TestRecoverySkipsBadRuns|TestBackgroundError' and watch each fail.
2. internal/daemon/runs.go:67-74 managedRun: add failure error.
3. runs.go:134-139 recoverRuns: on a Reconcile error keep the run: d.runs.runs[rec.ID] = &managedRun{engine: e, failure: err}. Keep the stderr line at :136.
4. runs.go:294-313 launchRun: reset r.failure = nil with r.result at :299. In the goroutine, after result.err = err (:307), set r.failure = err unless errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), so an owner stop that cancels a job (runs.go:337-338) is not an error.
5. internal/source/source.go:154-163 EngineRun: add Error string `json:"error,omitempty"` (proposed wire field).
6. runs.go:417-461 engineRuns: fill Error from the managed run when it is not busy.
7. internal/tui/overview.go:101-107: after the denials part, append "error: "+r.Error when set. Retry and stop keep working on the row.
8. internal/cli/daemoncmds.go:48-57: print "  error: ..." under the run.
9. Mutation-check: remove step 4's assignment and confirm TestBackgroundErrorStaysOnTheWireRow goes red; restore.
10. Docs: docs/state.md:168-175 (engine display snapshot) gets the error field; say it is daemon memory only and is not in run.json. docs/dashboard.md:106-110 gets the error text.
A run that failed to reconcile and is kept in the manager does not count as active: it does not block idle exit or daemon stop without --force (runs.go:166-176, :184). It still shows with its error, and stop and retry still work. Test: a daemon holding only a failed-to-reconcile run exits idle.

Line numbers above into internal/daemon/runs.go predate S05 (landed 67521b0, which moved recoverRuns to :118-157 and launchRun to :389-417); find them again before editing. S05 also keeps a recovered queued run in the manager without Reconcile.
Folded in from the S05 review: the unregistered-project skip in recoverRuns (:136-139) follows the same keep-and-show rule as a failed Reconcile. Open: engine.Load needs a registry.Project (engine.Load(d.runDeps(p), p, r)), and there is none for a removed project, so how a stop works for such a run is not decided. Candidates: stop it from the stored record alone, or leave it visible with the error and no actions. S38 (projects rm refuses while the project has unfinished runs) makes this state rare. The owner decides.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- go test -race -count=1 ./internal/daemon ./internal/source ./internal/tui ./internal/cli
- go test -race -count=1 ./... (the daemon and status changes reach the TUI and CLI tests)
- go vet ./...
- gofmt -l .
- slicer check
- adj lint
- Run the specific tests by name: TestRecoverySkipsBadRuns, TestBackgroundErrorStaysOnTheWireRow, TestRecoveredRunCanBeStoppedAndActiveRunIsPaused, TestDaemonStopRefusesBusyUnlessForced (lifecycle_test.go:124).
- Look at: any golden that lists engine rows (engine-*.txt) must still match: the error part only appears when Error is set.
